target_customer: Consumers with curly, wavy and coily hair, selling direct online and through retail such as Walmart
problem: Women with textured hair found store products drying and damaging, and wanted fresh, natural deep conditioners.
business_model: Direct to consumer subscription and online store for frozen, fresh ingredient hair treatments, plus mass retail wholesale
product_category: Natural textured hair care, frozen deep conditioners

founders.name: Muhga Eltigani
founders.background_notes: Company story says the brand began in her Philadelphia kitchen after she cut her hair and made her own recipes. Education not found in opened sources. One search snippet described the company as co-founded with Sam Roberts, but no opened company source says so, so not listed.

competitors.name: Mielle Organics
competitors.what: Natural textured hair care brand started in a kitchen, DTC first
competitors.traction_then: described by Forbes in 2019 as one of the fastest growing natural hair care companies in the US

competitors.name: Briogeo
competitors.what: Prestige texture-inclusive hair care sold through Sephora and DTC
competitors.traction_then: founded 2013, best known for its Don't Despair, Repair line

technical_complexity.rationale: Formulation and cold chain shipping of fresh ingredient products were the hard parts; no novel technology.

defensibility.rationale: Recipes and frozen format were copyable, crowded natural hair market; defensibility rests on brand and retail relationships.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied it in sources found; the main investor was Sundial founder Richelieu Dennis through New Voices Fund.

market_need_then: Large unmet demand among Black women for natural hair products; the founder said commercial products left her hair dry and damaged, and friends asked for her recipes.

identity.mascot_or_character: Ivy, a hair guide, and Olive, a tips character, per the company site
identity.visual_style: food themed, avocado and fresh ingredient imagery
identity.voice_and_tone: Warm, encouraging and playful; tagline Be Deliciously You

branding.brand_signature: Frozen avocado based treatments and the rewards currency called Avocados

rebrands.why: Not stated; the site now uses NaturAll Curl Club

branding.community_and_virality: Forbes 30 Under 30 2017 and Inc 30 Under 30 2018 recognition for the founder per search results; press coverage of the founder and funding

brand_strength.rationale: Distinct food themed identity with characters and loyalty program, national retail placement in Walmart, and wide founder press, but a modest scale overall.

outcome_analysis: NaturAll Club grew from a kitchen recipe business into a frozen hair treatment brand, took reported investment from Richelieu Dennis of New Voices Fund in 2019 and reached 4,500 Walmart placements by February 2025. It is active with a team of 17. Strong founder story, distinctive brand and retail partnership explain survival, while total funding and revenue are not public.
notes: SeedTable lists a seed of 1.6M with two investors and CB Insights lists a total of 1.65M with Y Combinator, New Voices Fund, 43North and Village Capital; both conflict with NewsOne's report that Dennis later added 4M. These aggregator figures are unverified and not recorded as rounds. The date of the 4M addition is unknown (article of 2019-11-03 mentions it). Founding year varies: 2015 in press release and NewsOne, 2017 on the company site. Competitor sources are 2019-dated search-result summaries and the Beauty Independent page was not opened. No outcome news found; the 2025 Walmart release shows the company active.
